claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a single-phase FCC baseline under the proposed processing conditions.
Replacing 5–10 at.% Ni with Al increases atomic-size mismatch in CoCrFeMnNi.
Replacing 5–10 at.% Ni with Al increases local lattice distortion.
Replacing 5–10 at.% Ni with Al increases short-range-order fluctuations.
The proposed short-range-order fluctuations are induced by atomic-size mismatch between Al and the original alloying elements.
Greater atomic-size mismatch produces enhanced local strain fields.
The enhanced local strain fields impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion enhances solid-solution strengthening.
Al-substituted alloys will have higher hardness than identically processed undoped CoCrFeMnNi.
Al-substituted alloys will have higher strength than identically processed undoped CoCrFeMnNi.
Within the single-phase FCC stability range, hardness and strength will correlate linearly with the degree of lattice distortion.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening can be used as evidence of local lattice distortion in these alloys.
The proposed strengthening relationship is limited to compositions that retain a single-phase FCC structure without phase segregation, clustering, or secondary phases.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes alloys exhibiting phase segregation or clustering, but the falsification rule treats segregation or clustering without mechanical improvement as falsifying evidence. Such an observation is outside the hypothesis's stated validity domain and therefore cannot, without qualification, serve as a decisive falsifier.
